📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1311 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Hugging Face ↗ Open Full Page

Building on Nemotron 3.5 Parse: Open Data, Fine-Tuning, and Faster Inference

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1311 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Hugging Face

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • We recently released NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Parse, a compact document model that turns page images into structured data for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and agents.
  • In a recent development, now we’re building on that release with synthetic training datasets, a fine-tuning recipe, and a DFlash2 speculator for faster inference.
  • Parse extracts content from pages of documents into reading order, assigns content classes such as headings, paragraphs, tables, and charts, and returns bounding boxes that locate the content.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We recently released NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Parse, a compact document model that turns page images into structured data for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and agents.

In a recent development, now we’re building on that release with synthetic training datasets, a fine-tuning recipe, and a DFlash2 speculator for faster inference. We’re also sharing how we trained Parse 3.5: first teaching document understanding through supervised fine-tuning, then using reinforcement learning to improve accuracy, consistency, and reliable completion.

Parse extracts content from pages of documents into reading order, assigns content classes such as headings, paragraphs, tables, and charts, and returns bounding boxes that locate the content. Tables and charts become structured records that can power downstream document processing applications.

Recent findings suggest that figure 1. Actual model output from a synthetic operations brief, showing the connection between the page and its structured representation.

According to recent reports, this latest version of Parse significantly extends its ability to read charts and tables, especially in more difficult and ambiguous cases. For example, bar charts or other plots that do not have any marked numeric values. The model is able to infer values by looking at the axes and height of the bar to derive these. Tables can be especially tricky because the structure is so meaningful, a shifted row or column can totally change the interpretation and meaning. These advancements have been largely powered by synthetic data generation, rendering variations of charts and tables with known ground truth and then training our model to reverse this process.

We are open-sourcing three datasets used in the Parse 3.5 training:.

Synthetic Charts V1 — 9.98M examples: rendered charts and structured annotations for learning categories, series, and numerical values.

Synthetic Tables V1 — 1M examples: rendered HTML tables with targets that preserve rows, columns, headers, and cell relationships.

OCR Synthetic Multilingual v2 — 7.9M examples: synthetic document pages with Parse-format targets across varied fonts and layouts, for multilingual OCR and structured page reading.

It has been revealed that each release includes images, annotations, generation documentation, and the training format. Use these pairs to fine-tune document models or create latest variations for a target document type or language.

Industry observers note that figure 2. Parse recovers 18, 27, 39, and 54 from the chart geometry.

Recent findings suggest that we trained Parse 3.5 with two phases of training. Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) spanning text, layout, tables, charts, and multilingual documents. Learning to predict structured targets established the general capability of reading a page and representing its contents.

We then continued with reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR), using Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO). Rewards check the quality of sampled extractions. For example, a chart extraction can earn a better reward for recovering the correct series and values, producing a usable structure, and finishing without repeatedly generating the same content.

A difficult page can have several valid representations. These checks give the model flexibility to find a correct answer without prescribing one exact token sequence, while discouraging looping and unfinished output.

Figure 3. A controlled comparison of SFT and GRPO with matched evaluation settings. These are development checkpoints, separate from the final released model. Loop counts use a repetition check. Methods.

In a recent development, the matched comparison reveals the benefit: loop-flagged outputs fall from 126 to 29 pages—about 77% fewer—and outputs reaching the 9,000-token limit fall from 185 to 35. Overall score improves from 66.24 to 71.38, including +5.18 points in tables and +4.15 in charts.

Industry observers note that A parser must generate substantial text and structure for every page. Alongside the training work, we optimized how Parse 3.5 processes images and decodes those outputs.

Industry observers note that naViT preprocessing adapts the input shape to the page. A visual adapter compresses the image sequence, and the text decoder consumes it as a prefix, replacing encoder–decoder cross-attention. Grouped-query attention with eight key/value heads (GQA-8) reduces the decoder’s attention-cache memory.

Recent findings suggest that the built-in multi-token prediction (MTP) head supplies one-token lookahead. Our DFlash2 speculator goes further: a small draft model proposes up to 32 tokens ahead, and Parse verifies the proposals together. In the measured 32-token configuration, it averages about 14 accepted draft tokens, or roughly 15 output tokens of progress per verification step including the target token.

Industry observers note that figure 4. Native single-pass throughput on one H200, BF16, using the same 2,078 pages. Parse 2.0 uses one trial per point; Parse 3.5 demonstrates three-trial medians. Arrows show the gain from Parse 3.5 base to DFlash2. Measurement details.

In the native single-pass benchmark on one H200 in BF16, DFlash2 increased throughput 7.62× at concurrency 1 and 1.52× at concurrency 512, compared with Parse 3.5 with speculative decoding disabled. At 512, Parse 3.5 reaches 13.48 pages/s without speculation and 20.44 pages/s with DFlash2, versus 2.98 for Parse 2.0. Those are 4.53× and 6.86× the Parse 2.0 throughput, respectively.

Sources indicate that fast parsing gives us room to revisit difficult regions. Start with a full-page prediction, then add focused reprocessing where the document needs it:.

Single pass - Parse the full page once for text, layout, tables, and charts.

Industry observers note that double pass - use for dense tables and small chart details. Crop the table and chart regions found by the parser, re-parse them at higher detail, and merge the refinements into the page output.

Triple pass - Instead of only using the models full page parsing bounding boxes, use a second pass of the model in detection mode in order to get verification that all boxes have been accurately found and text has not been missed and re-extract any found charts or tables in a third pass.

It has been revealed that figure 5. Additional stages focus computation on difficult regions. Multiple crops can require multiple requests.

Recent findings suggest that in the published reference evaluation, double and triple pass add 2.18 and 2.46 ParseBench points over single pass. The additional work lets applications trade some throughput for better extraction in difficult regions. Reference results and serving measurements.

We are sharing a Parse fine-tuning recipe that takes developers through paired data generation, NeMo Automodel SFT, and NeMo RL GRPO, using vLLM to generate candidate answers.

In a recent development, the worked example uses a synthetic dental form with an odontogram: a chart showing teeth, planned procedures, and affected tooth surfaces. Before adaptation, Parse reads the printed tooth numbers but misses the intended procedure table. SFT teaches it to associate each marked tooth with a procedure and its placement on the tooth.

Figure 6. A recorded recipe example: after SFT, all six chart rows match the target. Full image and native training label.

Industry observers note that RLVR then reinforces accuracy and consistent completion. In the dental reference run, the estimated first-attempt success rate (sampled pass@1) rose from 0.00% for the base model to 95.85% after SFT and 96.58% after RLVR.

Recent findings suggest that figure 7. Matched evaluation on 256 held-out forms from the same synthetic generator, with eight samples per page. Success requires natural completion, exact chart content, and error-free normalized page text. Evaluation protocol.

According to recent reports, to adapt the recipe, supply your own image/label pairs and a verifier: checks that determine whether an extraction is correct. The included document reward components cover text fidelity, bounding boxes, tables, chart facts, and completion. Combine the components relevant to your task, add schema checks, and use completion and repetition checks to discourage looping or unfinished output.

We are excited that the community has extended and improved Parse for Thai, Persian/Farsi, and Arabic already and we hope that these additional datasets and fine-tuning recipes will help encourage these efforts and future models.

We thank Denis Ovchinnikov for his work on vLLM integration and independent performance validation, Oliver Holworthy for improving the fine-tuning recipe's runtime setup and reproducibility, and Bo Liu for technical review.

Industry observers note that arXiv:2611.33584v1 Announce Type: upcoming Abstract: Financial knowledge graphs (KGs) link information across sources to support risk assessment, investment research, asset recommendations, and forecasting. Large language models (LLMs) help build these graphs by extracting relationships from text and matching entities across records. Yet a workflow may still prescribe which sources to consult and which checks to run. If the chosen sources lack relevant evidence, even accurate extraction can leave a financial question unanswered. LLM agents can adapt the workflow as evidence emerges. They use the graph and earlier findings to decide where to look next, which claims to verify, and whether to revision a record for later use. This is the first survey devoted to how LLM agents reshape the construction, maintenance, and use of financial KGs. Our taxonomy covers Knowledge Graph Construction, Temporal Evolution, Verification, Reconciliation, and Admission, Adaptive Acquisition, and Knowledge Graph Usage. We examine how studies evaluate graph quality, agents' use of evidence, financial task outcomes, and reliability over time. These evaluations show that agents can recover evidence missed in an initial search and revise records as new information arrives. Three questions remain unresolved. How can an agent tell whether it has enough evidence for a financial decision? After a record is corrected, how can the agent identify which earlier conclusions need to change? Which relationships and rules can it reuse in a new graph or domain?

The Information Content of News Embeddings

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (225 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Arxiv

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read

arXiv:2611.33458v1 Announce Type: newly introduced Abstract: Does the predictive success of news embeddings reflect a better measure of news surprises or other sources of return predictability in text? We decompose news embeddings by content into event-category, firm-identity, and idiosyncratic components, and by timing into historical levels and current deviations. At short horizons, event categories account for most of the predictive power of embedding forecasts, and simple forecasts based on historical average returns after news in each event category outperform them. At longer horizons, firm information already present in earlier news coverage accounts for a substantial share of return predictability, even after residualization on firm characteristics. The dominance of event categories persists, and historical levels still contribute in the first months, when using a language model pretrained entirely before our sample period. For Llama-2, even embeddings constructed from news more than three years old predict returns at long horizons. However, its predictive advantage over RoBERTa is concentrated in firm identity and the historical level, and its advantage in these components largely disappears by its pretraining cutoff. A calibration highlights that pretraining memory, a source of look-ahead bias, can account for this pattern. Describing news more fully is not the same as measuring news surprises, and persistent return predictability from news text does not by itself establish slow incorporation of news into prices.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Follow ZDNET: Add us as a preferred source on Google.

It has been revealed that if you used the ParkMobile app to pay for parking at a meter several years ago, you might be getting a payment as a result of a data breach. Unfortunately, it’s probably not an amount you’d expect for the inconvenience of having your data exposed. And while it’s a comically low amount, don’t spend it all in one place, because, well…. You’re literally not allowed to.

Here’s what’s happening and why the ParkMobile data beach settlement is raising eyebrows online.

Also: Hackers stole 1 billion records from Salesforce customer databases with this simple trick – don’t fall for it.

Industry observers note that in 2021, hackers accessed sensitive data from more than 21 million ParkMobile customers, including license plate numbers, email addresses, phone numbers, and mailing addresses. The hackers didn’t get any payment information.

ParkMobile denied any wrongdoing but agreed to a settlement to avoid the cost and time of going to court. If you filed a claim, you could choose to get your payment in cash — up to $25. If you didn’t file a claim but you were still affected, you probably received an email this week with your alternative payment — $1.

“As part of the agreed resolution,” the email explained, “you are entitled to receive a benefit.” The email went on to say that the benefit is a $1 discount code for the ParkMobile app.

First, the payment is only good for credit towards ParkMobile service fees (not even the actual parking fee), so you have to park at a ParkMobile-owned lot to use your benefit. Second, you have to enter the code you received manually in your account. Third, you can’t use your $1 all at once.

Recent findings suggest that your code is good for 25 cents off a ParkMobile service fee, the email explained, and it can be used up to four times, equaling $1. When I searched a few ParkMobile lots near me, service fees were between $1.80 and $4.

Get the biggest stories in tech every Friday with ZDNET’s Week in Review newsletter.

Industry observers note that naturally, people who received the email were quick to criticize. Several Reddit posts appeared, with users pointing out that you had to pay significantly more than your benefit to actually use it, claiming the settlement was just a ploy for lawyers to get paid, and some saying they thought the email was a phishing attempt.

Customers who received a $1 code have one year to use it.

In a recent development, want to follow my work? Add ZDNET as a trusted source on Google.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Automated AI endpoint discovery and protection are now generally available, enabling you to discover language model (LLM), Model Context Protocol (MCP), and Agent2Agent (A2A) endpoints behind Amazon API Gateway, Application Load Balancers, and Amazon CloudFront across your AWS Organization and protect them using AWS WAF.
  • It has been revealed that discovery is available through the fresh API Gateway API Portal, which recognizes the AI endpoints among the APIs it discovers automatically from traffic logs and service configuration records, with no agents to deploy or logs to forward.
  • Protection is available through the new AWS WAF AI Security managed rule group, which protects your AI endpoints.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Automated AI endpoint discovery and protection are now generally available, enabling you to discover language model (LLM), Model Context Protocol (MCP), and Agent2Agent (A2A) endpoints behind Amazon API Gateway, Application Load Balancers, and Amazon CloudFront across your AWS Organization and protect them using AWS WAF.

It has been revealed that discovery is available through the fresh API Gateway API Portal, which recognizes the AI endpoints among the APIs it discovers automatically from traffic logs and service configuration records, with no agents to deploy or logs to forward. An undocumented, public-facing MCP server appears as a shadow API. For unprotected AI endpoints, customers can enable protection using WAF.

Protection is available through the new AWS WAF AI Security managed rule group, which protects your AI endpoints. AWS WAF implements protocol recognition and compliance checks to block malformed MCP and A2A messages. When you enable content inspection, the rule group calls Amazon Bedrock Guardrails InvokeGuardrailsCheck API to detect prompt injection, jailbreak attempts, harmful content in requests, and sensitive information in responses. You can use AI Security alongside other AWS Managed Rules or your own custom rules to protect your applications. Additional fees apply, and Amazon Bedrock charges separately for content inspection calls.

Together, API Portal and AI Security provide you a complete solution from discovery of all AI endpoints in your AWS environment to protecting them, without having to write any custom rules.

API Portal is available in 32 AWS Regions. See the Amazon API Gateway FAQ for the list. AI Security is available in the following AWS Regions: US East (N. Virginia), US East (Ohio), US West (Oregon), Europe (London), Europe (Stockholm), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), and Asia Pacific (Sydney).

To get started, see the following resources:.

AWS WAF AI Security in the AWS WAF Developer Guide.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that expect travel headaches from coast to coast this week.
  • A very active pattern draped across North America will keep the storm train running in the days ahead.
  • In a recent development, the stormy setup arrives at the peak travel time of the year in the US.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that expect travel headaches from coast to coast this week. Several rounds of disruptive weather sweep are likely to cause delays at airports and make for challenging driving conditions just in time for the Thanksgiving long weekend.

A very active pattern draped across North America will keep the storm train running in the days ahead. Potent systems rolling into the West Coast will bring disruptions from Seattle to San Francisco, where high tides could swamp airport runways. East of the Rockies, a major coastal storm expected to develop on Wednesday will generate widespread heavy rain and winds so gusty there’s a “significant chance” the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade could be balloonless for the first time in 55 years. The same system will also deliver the season’s first measurable snow in some areas.

In a recent development, the stormy setup arrives at the peak travel time of the year in the US. The Transportation Security Administration screened 3.1 million passengers to close out the long weekend in 2025, marking the agency’s highest passenger volume on record. And with the extreme weather this week is set to sweep across some of the country’s biggest travel hubs, it could upend the best-laid travel intends.

A persistent series of low-pressure systems will drag waves of heavy precipitation into the Pacific Northwest throughout the week, making delays and the occasional cancellation likely for flyers in Seattle and Portland.

The real risk for delays begins to pile up when rain and gusty winds follow a cold front into northern California on Tuesday night Though the worst of the rain will likely clear out in time for the bulk of Wednesday’s travel, flooding is still a major concern for low-lying highways and parts of San Francisco International Airport.

Recent findings suggest that forecasters expect a near-record king tide—that is, one of the highest tides of the year—on Tuesday and Wednesday. King tides are a normal occurrence, but this year’s will be exacerbated by record-high sea levels driven by the Super El Niño. The climate phenomenon has pushed warm water toward the coast, which takes up more space than cold water.

Monday’s forecast from the National Weather Service called for a high tide of 8.5 feet at the San Francisco gauge on Wednesday morning, which is just shy of the all-time record of 8.66 feet set in January 1983, another Super El Niño year.

Farther east, the atmospheric ingredients are lining up for a sprawling nor’easter to develop over the Southeast by Wednesday and move north through Newly introduced England by the end of the week.

In a recent development, widespread heavy rainfall will accompany the storm northward, potentially worsening highway traffic as commuters and vacationers alike navigate slick roads in gloomy conditions. Gusty winds will reduce visibility during heavy rainfall. Forecasters expect several inches of rain along the East Coast, especially along the Interstate 95 corridor between South Carolina and New York.

Airline delays are almost certain given the dreaded mix of precipitation, low clouds, and stiff winds. The greatest impacts are likely in Charlotte and Raleigh in North Carolina on Wednesday, followed by Washington, DC, Philadelphia, Newly introduced York, and Boston on Thursday.

Industry observers note that all these cities are home to major hubs for various airlines. Foul conditions at one of those airports can have ripple effects that lead to delayed or canceled flights down the line, including in cities where the weather is just fine. This may be the most impactful Thanksgiving weather since a nor’easter rolled up the East Coast on the Wednesday and Thursday of the holiday weekend in 2014. That storm hit the major hubs with high winds and heavy rain, as well as up to a foot of wet snow across much of the interior Northeast. The event led to thousands of cancelled and delayed flights. (The US also got a taste of travel trouble earlier this month when a Federal Aviation Administration ground stop left travelers stranded.).

Industry observers note that the conditions could get so dire, that the Macy’s parade could go on but sans balloons. The parade will ground its balloons if there are sustained winds of 24 mph or gusts of 35 mph. The National Weather Service issued a high wind watch for Fresh York City beginning Thursday morning, with winds of 25 to 35 mph with gusts up to 60 mph possible, though when the nor’easter reaches New York will determine if the winds cross that crucial threshold during the parade.

Cold air wrapping into the western side of the same storm system could lead to the first measurable snow of the season throughout portions of the Midwest. Computer models are still a bit wishy-washy on exactly where and how much snow will fall, as the rain-snow line will depend on the precise track of the storm. As of Monday, the general consensus for a few inches of wet snow appears to focus on the St. Louis metro area east into central Illinois.

There’s some good news for travelers in the eastern US, at least: The nor’easter is expected to clear out by Saturday morning, which should hopefully reduce any snarls for travelers headed home on Sunday.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • AWS WAF now offers simplified pricing that follows what you protect instead of how you configure it.
  • Industry observers note that the fresh model makes protection costs predictable before you deploy.
  • According to recent reports, AWS WAF's upcoming pricing is effective from Feb 1, 2027 in all AWS commercial Regions, including Cape Town, Hong Kong, Hyderabad, Jakarta, Malaysia, Melbourne, Mumbai, New Zealand, Osaka, Seoul, Singapore, Sydney, Taipei, Thailand, Tokyo, Calgary, Frankfurt, Ireland, London, Milan, Paris, Spain, Stockholm, Zurich, Tel Aviv, Sao Paulo, N.

AWS WAF now offers simplified pricing that follows what you protect instead of how you configure it. Previously, you paid separate charges for each web ACL, rule, rule group subscription, and capacity tier, making every security decision a billing calculation. Now, your bill follows three dimensions: the resources you protect, the traffic AWS WAF inspects, and the level of protection you apply. This makes the cost-benefit trade-off easy to understand, and adding or changing rules no longer changes your rate. This new pricing goes into effect on Feb 1, 2027.

Industry observers note that the fresh model makes protection costs predictable before you deploy. Each web ACL now includes up to 2,500 WCU at no extra charge, up from 1,500, and you can add rules such as Bot Control common protections or the Anti-DDoS rule group without additional fees. You pay a resource fee for each protected resource, a base request fee for every request AWS WAF inspects, and a premium request fee only for traffic evaluated by advanced protections like Bot Control targeted protections, Fraud Control, API Security, and AI Security.

According to recent reports, AWS WAF's upcoming pricing is effective from Feb 1, 2027 in all AWS commercial Regions, including Cape Town, Hong Kong, Hyderabad, Jakarta, Malaysia, Melbourne, Mumbai, New Zealand, Osaka, Seoul, Singapore, Sydney, Taipei, Thailand, Tokyo, Calgary, Frankfurt, Ireland, London, Milan, Paris, Spain, Stockholm, Zurich, Tel Aviv, Sao Paulo, N. Virginia, Ohio, N. California, Oregon, as well as in AWS GovCloud, China Regions, and AWS Isolated Regions.

To learn more, visit the AWS WAF pricing page and review the AWS WAF Developer Guide as well as the blog post AWS WAF pricing now follows what you protect, not how you configure it.

#35874. Breaking: Anthropic Created a Honeypot to Lure AI Agents Into Misbehaving

Breaking: Anthropic Created a Honeypot to Lure AI Agents Into Misbehaving

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (666 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: WIRED

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Leather-clad billionaires aren’t the only ones who can be led astray by alleged honeypots.
  • Researchers at Anthropic have developed Siren, a fresh honeypot test for artificial intelligence agents.
  • It has been revealed that the test lets agents loose inside one of 26 different simulated sandbox environments.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Leather-clad billionaires aren’t the only ones who can be led astray by alleged honeypots.

Researchers at Anthropic have developed Siren, a fresh honeypot test for artificial intelligence agents. The setup puts agents in realistic simulations designed to tempt them into misbehaving. How they respond will help researchers evaluate the likelihood that new models will go rogue when deployed in the real world, as well as the effectiveness of different safety measures.

It has been revealed that the test lets agents loose inside one of 26 different simulated sandbox environments. Various features of the sandbox are deliberately misconfigured to allow egress, while an enticing file containing things like passwords and apparent routes onto the internet sits just outside the sandbox boundary. The setup then presents tasks that tempt the agent to reach outside the sandbox without giving it explicit permission to do so. Crucially, the sandbox exists inside a second sandbox that’s cut off from the outside world to avoid real-life mishaps.

“Models are going to continue getting better, continue finding zero-day vulnerabilities,” states Darya Kaviani, a researcher at Anthropic who specializes in security and helped develop Siren.

A zero-day vulnerability is a previously unknown flaw in a piece of software that can be used to pilfer data or gain unauthorized access. Anthropic’s Mythos models are especially skilled at finding zero-day bugs because they lack the guardrails that normally block this kind of potentially malicious activity.

Kaviani indicates we should assume AI models will become increasingly capable of finding and exploiting zero-days or figuring out other ways to break free from their constraints. The question then becomes whether they’ll resist the temptation to do so.

AI agents—models that perfect actions autonomously—are becoming increasingly commonplace. They power capable coding agents like Claude Code and Codex, as well as peppy personal assistants like Meta’s Muse and OpenAI’s Dots.

Recent findings suggest that but the rise of helpful agents has been accompanied by some remarkable bad behavior. Agents tested by Anthropic, OpenAI, and others have broken free from sandboxes and even hacked into other companies in an effort to solve challenging problems.

Industry observers note that assuming AI models continue to display such ingenuity, Kaviani claims it will be crucial to do more than just patch software. “Even as we strengthen our infrastructure, models will be able to also keep up and be able to find vulnerabilities,” Kaviani says.

According to recent reports, earlier versions of Claude are much more likely to fall into the honeypot trap than newer models, according to test runs with Siren. The more recent models have been given additional training designed to make them less likely to break the rules when performing agentic tasks.

“We’ve added this in both our supervised learning sets and a few reinforcement learning environments,” says Oscar O’Rahilly, an Anthropic researcher who specializes in AI training and who helped develop Siren. “This could be a driving factor for why it has improved so much.”.

Recent findings suggest that O’Rahilly states that models reason about whether to give in to temptation, which may partly explain why smarter models are less likely to break bad. Siren experiments also demonstrated that giving Claude a simple additional piece of text explaining that it should not escape the sandbox resulted in drastically fewer efforts to break free.

In Anthropic’s tests, Claude 5.5 and Claude Mythos 5.2 fell for the honeypot between 0.6 and 1.6 percent of the time. Two earlier models, Claude Mythos 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5, went rogue 12.7 percent and 25.8 percent of the time, respectively.

AI models are sometimes known to behave better if they know they’re being tested. But O’Rahilly says other experiments suggest that Claude actually behaves more responsibly if it thinks a scenario is real rather than a test.

As AI models get ever smarter, many researchers worry about whether they’ll outwit their human counterparts. If that does happen, then it may be essential that agents—and not just the executives responsible for them—can resist temptation.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, you can now run OpenSearch version 3.9 on Amazon OpenSearch Service.
  • It has been revealed that this release adds a new half-float vector type and a bf16 encoder, which store each vector dimension in 16 bits to reduce the memory and storage your vector indexes need.
  • Industry observers note that openSearch 3.9 also adds gRPC streaming for model predictions and agent execution.

According to recent reports, you can now run OpenSearch version 3.9 on Amazon OpenSearch Service. OpenSearch 3.9 helps you reduce vector memory and storage, evaluate search quality with more large language model (LLM) providers, build more responsive AI agents, and control access to shared resources.

It has been revealed that this release adds a new half-float vector type and a bf16 encoder, which store each vector dimension in 16 bits to reduce the memory and storage your vector indexes need. New 2-bit and 4-bit scalar quantization lets you choose the right balance of compression and recall for each workload. Base64-encoded vector ingestion makes request payloads smaller, which speeds up bulk loading. In addition, radial search now uses a redesigned graph traversal to improve both recall and throughput. In Search Relevance Workbench, LLM-as-a-Judge now works with Amazon Bedrock and other LLM providers through ML Commons connectors. You can also retry failed documents, edit ratings, and reuse earlier judgments to reduce repeated LLM calls.

Industry observers note that openSearch 3.9 also adds gRPC streaming for model predictions and agent execution. Responses come back token by token, so your agentic applications can show answers as they’re generated. Finally, the new resource sharing and access control framework allows you to share resources such as anomaly detectors and machine learning models with specific customers and roles without granting broad access.

Sources indicate that openSearch 3.9 is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon OpenSearch Service is offered. To learn how to upgrade, see Upgrading Amazon OpenSearch Service domains in the Amazon OpenSearch Service Developer Guide.

Amazon SageMaker HyperPod now supports managed cluster extensions for Slurm clusters. You can install, configure, revision, and remove managed features through the SageMaker AI console or API. The first two extensions cover observability and user management. Earlier, every observability or user management change for HyperPod Slurm clusters meant editing lifecycle scripts and then replacing or rerunning nodes. Now, HyperPod manages these features for you, and you keep lifecycle scripts and custom AMIs for your organization's own software.

Industry observers note that for each extension, you declare a configuration. HyperPod validates it and applies it to every node, including nodes you add later. It then reports the extension's status and the health of each node. The observability extension collects node, GPU, Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA), Slurm job, and Slurm cluster metrics. It sends them to Amazon CloudWatch or Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus, and you can add Amazon Managed Grafana dashboards. The user management extension creates people and groups with the same IDs on every node. It also controls who can sign in with SSH and use sudo on each node type, with local users, Active Directory, or both.

It has been revealed that cluster extensions are available at no additional charge in all AWS Regions where Amazon SageMaker HyperPod is available. You pay only for the AWS resources you use. To learn more, see Cluster extensions in the Amazon SageMaker AI Developer Guide, read the launch blog, or visit the Amazon SageMaker HyperPod product page.

Today, Amazon API Gateway unveils API Portal, a new feature that discovers, governs, and documents the APIs and AI endpoints behind Amazon API Gateway, Application Load Balancer, and Amazon CloudFront across your AWS organization.

According to recent reports, many organizations can't see which APIs are running, which were never registered, which are no longer maintained, and which lack protection. API Portal builds a continuously updated inventory using AWS-side traffic logs and service configuration records, with nothing to install, no logs to forward, and no traffic to reroute, for a single account or your entire AWS organization.

Every discovered API starts as a shadow API until you choose to manage it. API Portal labels each API as public or private and identifies AI endpoints, including MCP servers, A2A servers, and LLM endpoints. For managed APIs, it flags those that stop receiving traffic or lose their owner and evaluates security posture against best practices such as authentication, throttling, and AWS WAF protection. With AWS WAF API Security, it also shows the security events detected per API.

You can publish any managed API in a documentation portal for internal teams or external partners, with your branding, Amazon Cognito access control, and interactive Try it pages. If you already use API Gateway Portals, your portals continue to work and are now managed from the Documentation Portals section of API Portal.

API Portal is available in 32 AWS Regions; see the Amazon API Gateway FAQ and pricing pages for details.

To get started, see the following resources:.

Amazon API Gateway product page.

Introducing API and AI security on AWS blog.

AWS WAF API Security documentation.

In a recent development, AWS Sign-In now enables developers and AI agents to stay authenticated for up to 90 days without frequent sign-ins or consent prompts. With this launch, administrators can configure Sign-in duration, which controls how long an OAuth Sign-in session remains active, for individual IAM customers and roles.

This capability reduces authentication interruptions for long-running workflows and provides a more secure alternative to static access keys by using short-lived, renewable credentials. Existing session duration limits remain unchanged unless administrators explicitly configure longer durations.

Sources indicate that sign-In Duration supports AWS CLI (aws login), AWS MCP Server, and other OAuth-enabled applications. It does not affect AWS Management Console sessions. Customers can configure the setting using the IAM console, AWS CLI, or IAM API in all AWS commercial Regions.

To learn more, see the AWS Sign-In session management User Guide, Configure Sign-In duration on Role User Guide, Condition Key User Guide.

  • Recent findings suggest that during his first all-hands since returning as CEO, Huang acknowledged that he violated the firm’s policies and made some “very serious personal mistakes” that damaged his relationships with his wife and two children and prompted him to resign.
  • It has been revealed that huang spoke for about an hour, offering deeply personal thoughts about his therapy sessions and drawing applause at times from employees at Nvidia’s Silicon Valley headquarters as he spoke about the organization’s success and future.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang told employees on Tuesday that the firm’s code of conduct allows room for a “second chance,” that succession planning is a “flawed’ process,” and that he would work to rein in his “insanely intense” management style, according to remarks reviewed by WIRED.

Recent findings suggest that during his first all-hands since returning as CEO, Huang acknowledged that he violated the firm’s policies and made some “very serious personal mistakes” that damaged his relationships with his wife and two children and prompted him to resign. But he stated Nvidia’s board of directors made the appropriate decision for the company in welcoming him back. He added that the board made that call, not “the highest levels of our government.”.

It has been revealed that huang spoke for about an hour, offering deeply personal thoughts about his therapy sessions and drawing applause at times from employees at Nvidia’s Silicon Valley headquarters as he spoke about the organization’s success and future. He didn’t take any questions. While some Nvidia employees celebrated Huang’s return, others remained concerned about his behavior and the board’s decision to reinstate him.

It has been revealed that “This is going to be the hardest tech giant meeting I’ve ever done, and the second hardest meeting I have ever done,” Huang noted as he began to speak. “The hardest meeting I’ve ever done was with my wife.”.

Industry observers note that nvidia’s board accepted Huang’s resignation earlier this month, citing concerns about his personal behavior and lack of candor following news reports about extramarital affairs, including one with a woman accused of having ties to Chinese intelligence services. The very same board reinstated him on Monday, just 11 days later, after receiving fresh assurances from Huang and learning from the Trump administration that he was not under federal criminal scrutiny and his return would not be a risk to national security.

Sources indicate that huang and Nvidia, though, continue to face other legal and regulatory challenges. The board is investigating whether he was the target of foreign intelligence. US lawmakers expect him to testify before Congress next week. Lawsuits and other probes are ongoing into Nvidia’s disclosures about Huang’s behavior and its compliance with US export controls on chips.

Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Huang told staffers that he has been going to therapy “every day for an hour and a half” and that it’s “been helping me a lot.” He added that he “made some very serious personal mistakes. I hurt my family, I hurt my wife.”.

While Huang said he had never knowingly made a decision contrary to the manufacturer’s interests, he conceded that “in this one area” he had lacked “the courage” to disclose information that he knew would hurt his family, seemingly referring to the extramarital affairs.

Industry observers note that “The board and I spent the whole weekend together, and they, of course, they've been contemplating, and they've been collecting facts,” Huang noted. “They came to the judgment that they would like to invite me back as the CEO, to give me a second chance.”.

The CEO emphasized that Nvidia’s code of conduct, much of which he stated he wrote himself, still governs how employees are expected to treat one another and is intended to “create an environment that’s safe for people.”.

In a recent development, huang told employees that violations of the code would not be tolerated. But that “does not mean, the moment you violate a code of conduct, we walk you out the door,” he said. “Facts, circumstances, a lot of assessments” would factor in.

According to recent reports, “It has to always be evaluated in the context of the human,” he noted. “And this company has been more than gracious, more than thoughtful, more than fair in giving me a second chance.”.

It has been revealed that huang also pushed back against the notion that he had received preferential treatment because of his status in Silicon Valley. “There are rumors on the internet that apparently I’m a tech bro, and therefore I’m back,” Huang said. He rejected the suggestion that he was above the law or Nvidia’s code of conduct.

It has been revealed that later in the meeting, Huang addressed criticism of his self-described “deeply intense, insanely intense” management style, acknowledging that his behavior had at times negatively affected employees. While Huang maintained that the intensity he brings to his job elevates those around him, he conceded that he sometimes takes things too far.

Industry observers note that “It disempowers them, and that’s not right,” Huang said. The Nvidia CEO said he needed to figure out how to maintain his level of dedication to the manufacturer without hurting the people who work there.

“I need to hold myself to a higher standard at this time,” Huang remarked. He said that he would undergo a 360-degree performance review, soliciting feedback as often as monthly from people who work with him. The CEO added that he would be the first and only person at Nvidia to undergo such a review and that he did not want to institute the practice companywide.

Huang acknowledged during the meeting that Trump was a vocal supporter of Nvidia but insisted that politics played no role in how the company operated. “It is absolutely true that President Trump really, really loves our company,” Huang noted. “He is my president. And I’ll do everything I can to help this president.”.

Huang noted he would take the same approach with future US presidents. “We are the most apolitical manufacturer,” he said. “I don’t love that we talk about politics here. I love that we talk about work here.”.

Huang also sought to reassure women at Nvidia, describing himself as “one of our greatest advocates for creating an environment for women” and touting the company’s flexible work policies, which he said allow employees to simultaneously build their families and careers.

“If I did anything that put that in jeopardy, I cannot tell you how sad I am, and I’ll do everything I can to fix it,” Huang mentioned.

After Huang’s resignation, he and the tech giant’s board received criticism from Wall Street for not having an obvious internal successor in line. Huang addressed the matter head-on during the company meeting. “I don't believe in succession planning; I think it’s flawed,” he mentioned, specifying that the concept may make sense but the implementation often causes challenges.

Huang described each of his 60 reports as CEOs of their own units who could step up when he eventually leaves. “It creates resilience, and it creates the opportunity, which is ultimately the responsibility of the board, to give them the opportunity to decide at that time what the world needed, what the company needed, and be able to choose from a large collection of amazing people,” he said.

The CEO also argued that his brief absence had demonstrated Nvidia’s ability to operate without him. “I promise you, whether I’m here or not, this manufacturer is wired up to execute, execute, and execute,” Huang said.

Sources indicate that amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) for SQL Server now supports up to 500 databases per DB instance, up from the previous limit of 100. This higher density helps software as a service (SaaS) providers, multi-tenant applications, and other customers who run many databases on a DB instance. Previously, these customers had to spread their databases across several DB instances.

It has been revealed that you can use this feature to consolidate databases on fewer DB instances. This simplifies management, reduces the number of DB instances to monitor and patch, and lowers license and infrastructure costs. The 500-database limit applies to DB instances with 4 or more vCPUs (xlarge and larger, excluding burstable instance classes) on all SQL Server versions that Amazon RDS supports. It's available for Single-AZ deployments of Enterprise, Enterprise Developer, Standard, Standard Developer, and Web editions, and for Multi-AZ deployments of Enterprise, Enterprise Developer (using Always On Availability Groups), and Web edition.. Multi-AZ deployments using Database Mirroring, Multi-AZ deployments of Standard Edition, and smaller instances keep their current limits.

This feature is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon RDS for SQL Server is available. To learn more, see Amazon RDS for Microsoft SQL Server User Guide. For pricing details, see Amazon RDS for SQL Server Pricing.

Kalshi makes “difficult decision” to halt Utah trading after losing court fights

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Kalshi made the “difficult decision” to pause operations in Utah after losing a court fight to block the state’s ongoing enforcement actions under Utah gambling laws, Kalshi spokesperson Jacki McGavick stated Monday.
  • It seems Kalshi’s legal troubles in Utah have become too much for the prediction market platform to gamble on continued operations there.
  • Industry observers note that kalshi also wasn’t saved by an emergency motion from the Commodity Futures Trading Commission—which argues that the CFTC has exclusive jurisdiction over prediction market trading.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Kalshi made the “difficult decision” to pause operations in Utah after losing a court fight to block the state’s ongoing enforcement actions under Utah gambling laws, Kalshi spokesperson Jacki McGavick stated Monday.

It seems Kalshi’s legal troubles in Utah have become too much for the prediction market platform to gamble on continued operations there. In Utah, several lawsuits are still playing out, and Kalshi also lost a bid to persuade a federal appeals court to block those cases until the appeal is resolved.

Industry observers note that kalshi also wasn’t saved by an emergency motion from the Commodity Futures Trading Commission—which argues that the CFTC has exclusive jurisdiction over prediction market trading. At this time, the federal district court has not granted that motion to block Utah’s enforcement actions, either.

“This is an unfortunate outcome for the more than 177,000 Utahns who use Kalshi,” McGavick mentioned. “We will continue to fight this in court, and we look forward to returning to Utah once our legal position is vindicated.”.

Utah’s attorney general, Derek Brown, had filed both civil and criminal charges against Kalshi, as he defended the state’s 130-year ban on gambling.

In a press release discussing the initial lawsuit, he accused Kalshi of running “an online casino” that violates the state’s constitution. “Not only do our state laws ban gambling but Utah is one of only two states where gambling is also prohibited under the state constitution,” Brown said. “For 130 years, Utah has been clear: gambling has no place here, and we will enforce our laws.”.

Late Monday, a major Utah-area news outlet, KSL.com, reported that Brown was prepared to jail Kalshi’s co-founders, who had been summoned to be booked on 14 charges on December 5. He defended those looks, saying, “There is a question I have seen from people asking, ‘Well, do we modify this booking process if someone is a very wealthy and well-known tech billionaire?’ and the answer is ‘No, the process is the process; we don’t modify it based on who you are.’”.

However, on Tuesday, Utah decided to drop the criminal charges against Kalshi, McGavick confirmed to Ars. In a statement on X, Kalshi general counsel Yaakov Roth said, “We are pleased that Utah has chosen to dismiss criminal charges against Kalshi, while proceeding with civil litigation. Good faith jurisdictional disagreements should never be criminalized. We stand ready to work with State AGs on reasonable interim measures until courts resolve the dispute over who regulates prediction markets.”.

In a press release, Brown explained that the charges were dropped specifically due to the pause.

“Kalshi said it would geofence Utah, which blocks access to its site in the state,” the press release said. “The firm also committed to monitor for Utah-based IP addresses trying to reach its site. The Office then reevaluated its position and moved to dismiss the criminal case against the company and the individual defendants.”.

Brown threatened that the charges would be raised again if Kalshi tried to renew operations.

“Utah does not allow gambling, and prediction markets are gambling,” Brown mentioned. Kalshi has pulled out of Utah, and if it returns, so will the charges. Every manufacturer in this space should take note. If they promote, support, or enable gambling, we will hold them accountable.”.

Discussion of the Kalshi pause in a Utah sub-Reddit found some Redditors skeptical of the state’s cases as potentially overreaching.

However, many top commenters seemed pleased with the enforcement efforts, suggesting that Utah may have bipartisan support among some residents. One commenter cheered on the attorney general’s efforts as “the one item in the Utah GOP’s agenda I can get behind,” while another agreed that “prediction markets are incredibly toxic and are manipulated against ordinary people.”.

Sources indicate that many complained that Kalshi ads flooded their social media feeds. Some suggested the state should focus on banning advertising of prediction markets, while potentially still allowing adults to trade on event contracts if they want to throw their “money away.”.

Fears of insider trading were also raised. One commenter laid out why prediction markets seem suspiciously designed to promote insider trading and other market manipulation:.

In a recent development, “I’m pretty libertarian and hate banning things. But gambling and prediction markets are a scourge. Even the term ‘prediction market’ is a misnomer. Because ultimately when people with big dollars get involved it creates a financial incentive for them to make fucked up things happen in the real world. Think about it, decades ago we understood that sports betting was a problem because it corrupted sports—something that ultimately is pretty meaningless. Then we got all these people betting on the stock market with puts and it created huge incentives to cause havoc with markets. Now if people are betting big money on politics and wars and everything else, it just means people with influence can make money by making improbable/unexpected things happen.”.

One commenter joked, “I wonder how Kashi would have reacted if the judge in charge of their case had ‘traded’ $500,000 on the event of them losing the case. Not a problem at all, right?”.

On the same day Kalshi unveiled its temporary pause in Utah, a judge rejected a request from Upcoming York Attorney General Letitia James to immediately shut down Kalshi in that state, Courthouse News reported.

Fresh York Supreme Court Justice Melissa Crane noted she was “uncomfortable” granting the temporary restraining order so early in the case because “there does seem to be an indication that there would be market disruption that I’m concerned about.” Kalshi attorney Grant Mainland described it a little differently, claiming that a sudden halt would cause a “market emergency.”.

Industry observers note that “I think this is the ultimate relief in the case, which is improper for me to do without full briefing,” Crane mentioned. Instead of granting James’ request, she recommended that Kalshi take steps to address the state’s top concerns by considering “safeguards for consumers between 18 and 20,” who are under the state’s legal gambling age, Courthouse News reported.

According to Kalshi’s estimates, Latest York’s Kalshi user base (1.5 million) is much larger than Utah’s, so the market disruption from the Utah shutdown may not have carried the same dire stakes for Kalshi or its broader user base.

It has been revealed that the CFTC has sought to intervene in that case, too, and it seems clear that Kalshi expects the questions of who can regulate prediction markets and what trading qualifies as a “bet” to reach the Supreme Court. Kalshi’s spokesperson did not respond to Ars’ questions on how the Utah pause broadly impacted users or the platform.

So far, “three federal appeals courts have ruled that states can regulate prediction markets, while a fourth found they cannot,” Courthouse News reported. But despite the current balance tipping toward allowing states to regulate prediction markets, Kalshi appears confident that the Supreme Court will resolve the disparate court rulings in its favor.

In a lawsuit filed by a disgruntled Kalshi user, Kalshi argued that it would waste lower courts’ time to continue litigating these cases and that no case should be resolved until the Supreme Court weighs in.

In that case, Kalshi user Scott Bright alleged that he lost more than $300,000 on sports bets that were technically illegal in Washington.

According to Kalshi, all of Bright’s claims rest “on the premise that state gambling laws reach KalshiEX’s federally regulated exchange—the question now before the Supreme Court. Plaintiff puts the cart before the horse; Defendants ask only that the Court let that threshold question be resolved first.”.

The court has yet to address Kalshi’s request to stay the case, but Bright has argued that Kalshi is trying to “sideline a case governed by binding Ninth Circuit precedent so that they can wait for a Supreme Court decision that may never come.”.

Sources indicate that kalshi did not respond to Ars’ request for a statement on Bright’s lawsuit. In their court filing, they argued that “a stay will let the Supreme Court address an glitch that could dispose of every claim, will not meaningfully harm Plaintiff, and will spare Defendants and the Court litigation under a framework that may soon be displaced.”.

iRestore Elite Laser Hair Growth System Review: Husband-Approved

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1360 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: WIRED

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It’s jarring, for example, when the luscious, flowing locks of your youth start to disappear before your very eyes.
  • Sources indicate that I learned about iRestore’s Elite Laser Growth Hair System after it came across my TikTok FYP.
  • It has been revealed that however, an even better test subject stood before me: my sweet husband, who is dealing with a rapidly receding hairline.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Aging Process is hard. It’s jarring, for example, when the luscious, flowing locks of your youth start to disappear before your very eyes. But there's nothing to do about this natural hair loss—or is there? While still the subject of ongoing research, red-light therapy has been used to treat inflammation, pain relief, and wrinkles, and—as it turns out—it may also help with hair regrowth. It’s also a much more accessible option than flying to Istanbul for a full-on hair transplant.

Sources indicate that I learned about iRestore’s Elite Laser Growth Hair System after it came across my TikTok FYP. My algorithm likely served it to me because of my own hair woes (scalp irritation and eczema). Upon learning more about the system, I hoped it could help me with cell regeneration and kill off the bacteria causing flares on my scalp.

It has been revealed that however, an even better test subject stood before me: my sweet husband, who is dealing with a rapidly receding hairline. So I roped him into testing this laser helmet—for science, of course. And to better understand stated science, I spoke with Zakia Rahman, MD, FAAD, a clinical professor of dermatology at Stanford University School of Medicine.

Red-light therapy didn’t start as a treatment for antiaging and recovery. It actually came about as an accidental solution for hair loss in the 1960s, when Hungarian scientist Endre Mester was researching whether exposure to red light could treat cancer in hairless mice. Imagine his surprise when the mice started growing hair.

Red-light therapy has come a long way since then. According to Rahman, red-light wavelengths are thought to activate the mitochondria in skin cells, which may encourage an uptick in the production of adenosine triphosphate (ATP) to promote fresh growth. Red-light therapy may also improve blood flow to hair follicles.

Importantly, iRestore's devices are FDA-cleared—a safety designation from the US Food and Drug Administration indicating that a product is “substantially equivalent” to another legally marketed device. There are three hair-growth devices in iRestore's lineup: the entry-level Essential ($425), the mid-tier Professional ($799), and the Elite ($1,699). Each contains iRestore’s proprietary Lumitech technology, which combines LED lights and medical-grade lasers. These laser diodes, called Vixo lasers, operate in the range of 655 to 680 nanometers (nm). (Preliminary studies with mice have shown that using red light in the 600- to 660-nm range, and infrared wavelengths in the 800- to 850-nm range, can promote cell regeneration, pain relief, and more.).

The idea is that this dynamic duo of lights and lasers can penetrate deeper into the skin than ordinary red light with lasers, while the LEDs ensure light is distributed across the scalp for maximum efficacy. Together, they reach a maximum of 2,500 milliwatts (mW) in the Elite, compared to the Professional's 1,410 mW and Essential's 600 mW.

According to recent reports, the Elite is iRestore’s top-of-the-line offering and has the most LEDs of the three laser hair-growth systems, with 500 diodes in total—that's 300 lasers and 200 LEDs. The Essential has 51 lasers and 69 LEDs for a total of 120 diodes, while the iRestore Professional has 82 lasers and 200 LEDs for a total of 282 diodes. The Elite was also designed to cover more of the scalp than the other two models and requires 12 minutes of daily use, while the Professional and Essential require 25 minutes every other day.

If price is not a factor, the Elite is the no-brainer choice due to its higher-concentrated light therapy, shorter use time, and potentially faster results.

Sources indicate that the helmet arrived in hefty red packaging containing the helmet, a portable battery pack (annoyingly, this is a $99 add-on purchase), a charging cord, and a red-and-black zippered travel case. It feels very fragile, and I wouldn't throw it around—then again, you probably wouldn't initiative to shove such an expensive device in the back of your bathroom vanity.

Industry observers note that during the daily 12-minute sessions with the Elite helmet, you'll feel as if you're sitting under bright, hot sunlight. The remote displays a countdown of how many minutes you have left, and it beeps once the cycle is complete. Because I was testing the helmet to treat my dry scalp and eczema, I grew increasingly concerned with every passing minute of feeling warmer and warmer. (Sweating is a big no-no for eczema, so I wasn’t thrilled to experience this side effect.) With time, my husband was able to get used to the heat-lamp effect, as it’s not painful, just initially uncomfortable.

It has been revealed that within the first two weeks of continuously using the helmet, I was thrilled to see baby hairs begin to pop up around my husband's hairline. The growth continued through two months of regular use. The top of his crown had more volume and overall hair density, while latest growth appeared in the more drastically affected areas near his forehead. While the additional hair didn’t completely cover his scalp, the change was stark enough for old college friends and family members to remark on how good his hair looked.

It has been revealed that the effects aren't permanent, though. Unfortunately, my husband stopped his iRestore routine after a few months due to travel. While the iRestore Elite comes with a case that makes it super portable, my husband was nervous about misplacing it while we were on the go. (Also, the thing takes up a decent amount of space.) Unfortunately, stopping the treatments reversed the progress in a matter of weeks. Just like that, he was back to square one.

In a recent development, rahman likens this phenomenon to the importance of a commitment to a healthy daily diet and regular exercise; one instance of either won't make a difference in your health. Rather, consistency is required to drive results. When I told her that my husband's hair growth had fallen off, she strongly encouraged us to pick it back up.

It has been revealed that in addition to using the red-light therapy helmet as recommended, iRestore suggests adding thickening haircare products (shampoo, conditioner, supplements, and serum) to your regimen to get the best results. The star ingredient in the serum and shampoo is plant-based Redensyl, which is meant to fortify hair follicles during their regrowth. Additional elements—like the shampoo's castor oil and biotin, and the conditioner's vegan keratin and argan oil—act as natural strengtheners.

The supplements contain natural dihydrotestosterone (DHT) blockers derived from saw palmetto. These blockers work to prevent the enzyme (5-alpha reductase) from transforming testosterone into DHT. In essence, this hormone is a driver of pattern hair loss and can lead to general inactivity in hair growth.

Recent findings suggest that the supplements, strengthening serum, shampoo, and conditioner come included with the purchase of the iRestore Elite. The extras didn't seem to boost my results but may have supported my husband's regular use of the helmet. (Full disclosure: He was also using his usual Rogaine throughout this entire process.).

According to recent reports, ultimately, these included products are a nice bonus, but you don't need to go out of your way to buy them from iRestore or to replenish your stash. Plenty of anti-hair-loss treatments are available, including oral and topical medications and hair-transplant procedures. All have their merits in slowing hair thinning and promoting fuller hair. Even so, “combination therapy will work better than a stand-alone," notes Rahman, in response to my question about whether red-light therapy could work as an isolated treatment or if it's best to include it as part of a multicomponent regimen. Essentially, the potential benefits of red-light therapy only stand to increase when you supplement it with minoxidil and other highly researched hair-loss measures.

As for my eczema, the iRestore Elite did quell my scalp flare-ups, but I don't think I'd throw down so much money for just that. For hair regrowth, that's a totally different story. My husband was already using Rogaine before the iRestore Elite revealed up. But combined with the helmet and iRestore's hair-growth products and supplements, he experienced greater results. For those pursuing thicker hair at home, the iRestore Elite is surprisingly effective.

#35860. How brewers can protect beers from smoke-tainted hops

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (925 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Ars Technica ↗ Open Full Page

How brewers can protect beers from smoke-tainted hops

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (925 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that the 2020 Oregon wildfires burned over 1 million acres, destroyed thousands of structures, and killed 11 people.
  • Industry observers note that that’s why Oregon State University (OSU) scientists have been studying how brewers could offset the negative impacts of smoke taint while still incorporating affected hops in their brews.
  • As previously reported, the chemistry of brewing beer is a very active area of research.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the 2020 Oregon wildfires burned over 1 million acres, destroyed thousands of structures, and killed 11 people. Smoke from the fires spread across the entire region; this “smoke taint” adversely affected not only local wine production, but also hops grown for beer brewing. Since the Pacific Northwest produces more than 95 percent of US hops and about 40 percent of the global supply, the potential economic impact is significant.

Industry observers note that that’s why Oregon State University (OSU) scientists have been studying how brewers could offset the negative impacts of smoke taint while still incorporating affected hops in their brews. Most recently, they found that it all depends on the quantity of tainted hops that are included and when hops are added during the brewing process, according to a fresh paper published in the Journal of the American Society of Brewing Chemists.

As previously reported, the chemistry of brewing beer is a very active area of research. For instance, in 2018, OSU chemist Thomas Shellhammer—who also co-authored this latest paper—identified the growing popularity of “dry hopping” (adding hops after fermentation, common for pale ales) among craft brewers as the likely culprit of the exploding beer bottle phenomenon.

Sources indicate that all beer contains hops, a key flavoring agent that also imparts useful antimicrobial properties. (Beer spoils quickly without them.) Brewers mash and steep grain in hot water, which converts all that starch into sugars. This is traditionally the stage where hops are added to the liquid extract (wort) and boiled to give the beer that hint of bitterness. During the boiling process, a portion of the resins (alpha acids) in hops isomerize into iso-alpha acids. That chemical rearrangement of the molecules is what produces bitterness. Yeast is then added to trigger fermentation, turning the sugars into alcohol.

In a recent development, far from being the chemically inert ingredient brewers have long assumed, hops contain starch enzymes that, under certain conditions, can boost their activity to such a great extent that excessive re-fermentation occurs (“hop-creep”) after bottling. Dry-hopped beers produce significantly higher CO2 levels and packaging pressures, because there is much more re-fermentation going on than usual. And sometimes that pressure builds until the bottle explodes.

In a recent development, in the wake of the 2020 wildfires, Shellhammer turned his attention to smoke-tainted hops. The primary culprit is volatile phenols (VP), which are produced when the lignin in plant cells is exposed to the high heat of a wildfire. Earlier this year, the OSU team discovered that smoke exposure while the hops are drying increased VP uptake and substantially altered the hops’ aroma; those with higher levels took on meaty, smoky, and artificial BBQ notes; medicinal flavors have also been reported. Those notes were so strong that they overpowered more desirable beery qualities, like citrus notes or aroma intensity.

In a recent development, for this latest project, Shellhammer worked with graduate student Cade Jobe to harvest Idaho-grown Cascade hops. Then they “smoked” the hops in kilns using wood pellets injected into the air intake systems, then dried them. They also harvested and dried non-smoked hops as a control.

Credit: Ellie Lafferty/Oregon State University Credit: Ellie Lafferty/Oregon State University.

Next, Shellhammer and Jobe brewed several batches of beer, blending smoke-tainted hops with untainted hops at different levels (25,  50, and 75 percent), along with beer brewed using only tainted hops and beer brewed with no tainted hops. They did this using both a dry-hopping process and one where they added hops during wort boiling. They measured the VP concentrations of each batch of beer with gas chromatography. Finally, a panel of 24 blind tasters evaluated each beer.

According to recent reports, shellhammer and Jobe found that dry-hopping with smoke-tainted hops resulted in increased VP concentrations; the more tainted hops were included, the higher those concentrations. The tasters reported more intense smoky aromas in those beers as well as meaty, smoky, medicinal, and artificial BBQ flavors.

Sources indicate that by contrast, when tainted hops were added during the boil, the resulting beer was pretty much indistinguishable from beers brewed with no smoke-tainted hops, even though the former still showed the same increases in VP concentrations. There was no discernible difference when hops were added during the wort boiling stage.

Sources indicate that the authors suggest brewers could blend smoke-tainted hops with untainted batches when dry-hopping, keeping the smoke-tainted hops to less than 50 percent. This would still allow brewers to use tainted batches of hops, reducing the economic impact of wildfires on beer production.

“Hop growers and brewers are looking for guidance on whether and how to use smoke-affected hops,” remarked Jobe. “This research begins to provide some practical information to help hop growers and brewers understand how smoky hops impact beer so that they can make the best decisions.”.

Sources indicate that there’s still more research to be done to confirm the precise ratios and to replicate these initial findings. Future research should also explore the impact of hops exposed to smoke under field conditions, when the plant is still metabolically active, along with consumer studies to evaluate whether beer drinkers more generally will find the flavors of beers made with blended hops (tainted and untainted) acceptable. The findings may not extend to wine production, however, since the fermentation processes are so different, per the authors. And grapes comprise almost all the raw materials in wine, while hops are a smaller fraction of beer brewing ingredients.

Journal of the American Society of Brewing Chemists, 2026. DOI: 10.1080/03610470.2026.2749166  (About DOIs).

Amazon discovers Falcon 9 and Ariane 6 can deliver when nobody else can

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A European Ariane 6 launcher propelled 36 satellites into orbit for the Amazon Leo broadband constellation Tuesday, continuing the network’s build-out after 40 satellites were lost earlier this month during a failure of United Launch Alliance’s Vulcan rocket.
  • The launch was an key rebound for Amazon, bringing the Amazon Leo fleet to 432 satellites as the manufacturer seeks to fill the void left by the grounding of ULA’s Vulcan rocket, Amazon’s primary launch provider.
  • According to recent reports, the next Falcon 9 launch for Amazon Leo is now planned for December, Amazon remarked, moved forward from its previous launch date next year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A European Ariane 6 launcher propelled 36 satellites into orbit for the Amazon Leo broadband constellation Tuesday, continuing the network’s build-out after 40 satellites were lost earlier this month during a failure of United Launch Alliance’s Vulcan rocket.

The launch was an key rebound for Amazon, bringing the Amazon Leo fleet to 432 satellites as the manufacturer seeks to fill the void left by the grounding of ULA’s Vulcan rocket, Amazon’s primary launch provider. Now, an Amazon official tells Ars it is accelerating several Falcon 9 introduces the company has purchased from SpaceX, which also owns the Starlink satellite network that Amazon seeks to dethrone.

According to recent reports, the next Falcon 9 launch for Amazon Leo is now planned for December, Amazon remarked, moved forward from its previous launch date next year. Several more Falcon 9s are scheduled to launch Amazon Leo satellites in rapid succession after the December flight.

It has been revealed that amazon cast a wide net when it started signing deals for launch services five years ago, securing rides on 108 flights with every available medium- or heavy-lift rocket in the West to place a fleet of 3,232 satellites into low-Earth orbit. As of Tuesday, Amazon and its launch partners have completed 17 of those flights, with one mission failure.

Industry observers note that amazon executives initially bought up capacity from US-based United Launch Alliance, Europe’s Arianespace, and Blue Origin. Nearly all of those launch contracts depended on rockets still in development: ULA’s Vulcan, Europe’s Ariane 6, and Blue Origin’s New Glenn.

Recent findings suggest that each launch vehicle faced development delays, as all new rockets do. New Glenn has been grounded since May after an explosion on Blue Origin’s launch pad in Florida. ULA’s Vulcan will be sidelined for months after misfiring during a mission with Amazon satellites on November 15.

Sources indicate that amazon started booking launches in 2023 with SpaceX. Falcon 9 successfully rolled out Amazon’s first three missions last year, each with 24 satellites. Amazon soon reserved 10 more flights on SpaceX’s Falcon 9 rocket as delays mounted with Amazon Leo’s other launch providers, especially ULA and Blue Origin.

The relationship between Amazon and SpaceX is a peculiar one. Amazon aims to catch up to SpaceX’s Starlink network, now boasting more than 11,000 satellites, to bring competition to the satellite broadband market. Federal regulators approved Amazon Leo’s second-generation constellation earlier this year, an addition that will bring the fleet to more than 7,000 satellites in the 2030s. Amazon also looks a direct-to-device service, joining SpaceX and others in the pursuit of consumer demand for mobile connectivity.

But Starlink is far ahead. SpaceX has repurposed the Starlink satellite design for use on several US military programs, and Starlink rolls out on Falcon 9 are winding down as SpaceX’s Starship enters service. Starship is capable of launching heavier, more powerful Starlink satellites, a culmination that will only widen the gap with Amazon and other competitors in the satellite Internet business.

Recent findings suggest that starlink’s move to Starship opens up launch slots on Falcon 9, allowing Amazon to accelerate its launches with SpaceX in the near term. But SpaceX doesn’t strategy to keep Falcon 9 around for long. The company has reportedly stopped accepting commercial Falcon 9 bookings after 2028.

In a recent development, that means Amazon Leo needs its other launch providers to step up. Arianespace is doing so, with four successful Ariane 6 flights for Amazon this year. Amazon reserved six additional flights with Arianespace in September as Ariane 6 proved its mettle.

But there are questions about Europe’s ability to ramp up production of Ariane 6 rockets, which are single-use and not reusable like Falcon 9 and Upcoming Glenn. Europe’s rocket factories are sized to support a launch cadence of up to nine or 10 Ariane 6 flights per year. Arianespace will likely reach six Ariane 6 flights this year, with one more remaining before the end of December.

European taxpayers paid for development of the Ariane 6 and the industrial capacity to build the rockets, and they continue to subsidize each Ariane 6 flight, whether it carries a European government payload or commercial satellites for a large American corporation like Amazon.

European government ministers are mulling proposals to increase Ariane 6 production to meet surging demand from commercial customers and Europe’s internal space programs. A decision could come next month, but a ramp-up in launch cadence won’t happen overnight.

Sources indicate that amazon paid United Launch Alliance hundreds of millions of dollars for expansion at Cape Canaveral, Florida, to prepare for as many as 25 Vulcan launches per year. Such a launch cadence is a long way off for ULA, which has now introduced Vulcan five times (with one failure) in its three years of service.

Sources indicate that blue Origin, owned by Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, could resume Latest Glenn flights early next year after completing a launch pad rebuild. It is not clear when Amazon might begin launching on New Glenn, but finding slots in the rocket’s launch schedule could be difficult as Blue Origin prioritizes work for NASA’s Artemis lunar program.

Recent findings suggest that in the meantime, SpaceX will offer Amazon its most assured rides to space. Falcon 9s can launch from Cape Canaveral every few days, and Amazon is ready to tap into that capability with hundreds of satellites in storage waiting to go to orbit.

It has been revealed that here are some of the most striking things Huang said during the meeting, according to remarks reviewed by WIRED. Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

On self-improvement: “I go to therapy every day for an hour and a half. And it’s been helping me a lot.”.

“I also didn’t believe in succession planning. Let that sink in. I don’t believe in succession planning. I think it’s flawed. The idea of succession planning is not flawed. What people think succession planning means is flawed.”.

It has been revealed that “There’s a reason why we don’t have succession planning; it’s not because we are unaware of the word. I’m the longest-running tech CEO in history.”.

On politics: “There [were] also rumors that apparently I’m back because the highest levels of our government wanted me back. That is also completely untrue. Our board of directors performed their duty as they should have.”.

Recent findings suggest that “Don’t think for a second that politics ever plays a role in this company, not even a little bit. We are the most apolitical company. I don’t love that we talk about politics here. Take it home. I love that we talk about work here.”.
